title: Merton equity and debt value from asset value and volatility
deliverables: per-firm table [N]: E, B0, d1, d2
frame: DIKETAHUI: firms [N] with V, sigma_V, D (face), T, r. DITANYAKAN: equity E, debt B0 (same money unit). RUMUS: card Core 1, 3: d1 = [ln(V/D) + (r + sigma_V^2/2)T]/(sigma_V sqrt T), d2 = d1 - sigma_V sqrt T; E = V N(d1) - D e^-rT N(d2); B0 = V - E; toolkit merton_model(V, sigma_V, D, T, r). JAWAB: 1) units. 2) d1, d2. 3) E. 4) B0. 5) check E >= V - D e^-rT, B0 <= D e^-rT.
formulas: E = V N(d1) - D e^(-rT) N(d2)
B0 = V N(-d1) + D e^(-rT) N(d2)

title: Merton risk-neutral default probability and distance to default
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, sigma_V, D, T, r per firm. DITANYAKAN: DD (= d2) and PD = N(-d2). RUMUS: card Core 2: DD = [ln(V/D) + (r - sigma_V^2/2)T]/(sigma_V sqrt T); PD = N(-DD). JAWAB: 1) inputs per firm. 2) DD. 3) PD. 4) percent if asked. 5) check PD in (0,1), increasing in D/V, sigma_V.

title: Merton credit spread of risky debt
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, sigma_V, D, T, r. DITANYAKAN: debt value, yield y, spread s = y - r. RUMUS: card Core 3: B0 = V N(-d1) + D e^-rT N(d2); y = -(1/T) ln(B0/D); s = -(1/T) ln[N(d2) + V N(-d1)/(D e^-rT)]. JAWAB: 1) d1, d2. 2) B0. 3) y, s continuous per year. 4) bp = s x 10000. 5) check s >= 0.

title: Calibrating asset value and volatility from equity (Merton two-equation system)
deliverables: per-firm table [N]: V, sigma_V, DD, PD, residuals
frame: DIKETAHUI: E (market cap), sigma_E, D, T, r per firm. DITANYAKAN: V, sigma_V, then DD, PD, spread. RUMUS: card Core 1: solve E = V N(d1) - D e^-rT N(d2) and sigma_E E = N(d1) sigma_V V; start V0 = E + D e^-rT, sigma_V0 = sigma_E E/V0; toolkit merton_calibrate(E, sigma_E, D, T, r). JAWAB: 1) units (price x shares; debt same unit). 2) fsolve. 3) residuals. 4) DD, PD. 5) check V > E, sigma_V < sigma_E, equity reprices.

title: Real-world distance to default with physical drift
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, sigma_V, D, T, mu (asset drift) per firm, r. DITANYAKAN: physical DD and PD, plus risk-neutral for contrast. RUMUS: card Core 2, V3: DD_P = [ln(V/D) + (mu - sigma_V^2/2)T]/(sigma_V sqrt T); PD_P = N(-DD_P); toolkit merton_model(..., mu=mu). JAWAB: 1) mu from given or equity return. 2) DD_P. 3) PD_P. 4) PD_Q = N(-d2). 5) check PD_P < PD_Q when mu > r.
pitfalls: using r when the task says physical/real-world

title: KMV default point distance to default and EDF proxy
deliverables: per-firm table [N]: DPT, DD, EDF proxy
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, sigma_V (or E, sigma_E to calibrate), short-term debt STD, long-term debt LTD; optional empirical DD->EDF map. DITANYAKAN: DPT, DD, EDF. RUMUS: card Core 2, V2 (b): DPT = STD + 0.5 LTD; DD = (V - DPT)/(sigma_V V); EDF = empirical map, else N(-DD) proxy. JAWAB: 1) DPT. 2) calibrate with D = DPT if asked. 3) DD. 4) EDF via interpolation of map or N(-DD). 5) check DD decreasing with leverage.
pitfalls: N(-DD) reported as EDF without saying it is a proxy

title: Iterative KMV asset value time series (Vassalou-Xing)
deliverables: per firm: sigma_V, mu, DD, PD, iterations
frame: DIKETAHUI: daily equity values E_t [T], debt D, T, r_t. DITANYAKAN: V_t, sigma_V, DD at end. RUMUS: card completing: guess sigma_V = sigma_E; invert Merton E_t -> V_t (brentq each day); sigma_V = std(diff ln V, ddof=1) sqrt(252); iterate to |change| < 1e-4; mu = mean log return x 252 (+ sigma^2/2 if stated). JAWAB: 1) initial sigma. 2) invert. 3) re-estimate. 4) loop. 5) DD, PD with last V. 6) check convergence.
formulas: E_t = V_t N(d1) - D e^(-rT) N(d2), solve V_t

title: Naive distance to default (Bharath-Shumway)
deliverables: per-firm table [N]: sigma_D, sigma_V, naive DD, naive PD
frame: DIKETAHUI: E, sigma_E, F (face of debt), past-year equity return r_{i,t-1}, T. DITANYAKAN: naive DD and PD. RUMUS: card completing: sigma_D = 0.05 + 0.25 sigma_E; sigma_V = (E sigma_E + F sigma_D)/(E+F); mu = past return; DD = [ln((E+F)/F) + (mu - sigma_V^2/2)T]/(sigma_V sqrt T); PD = N(-DD). JAWAB: 1) sigma_D. 2) sigma_V. 3) DD. 4) PD. 5) check no solver used.

title: Equity volatility from prices then Merton pipeline
deliverables: per-firm: sigma_E, E, V, sigma_V, DD, PD, spread
frame: DIKETAHUI: daily prices [T] per firm, shares outstanding, debt, r, T. DITANYAKAN: full Merton outputs. RUMUS: card conventions: sigma_E = std(diff ln P, ddof=1) sqrt(252); E = last price x shares; then Core 1-3. JAWAB: 1) clean prices (drop NaN). 2) log returns. 3) sigma_E. 4) E. 5) calibrate. 6) DD, PD, spread. 7) check units of E and D match.
pitfalls: simple returns or ddof=0 when log returns ddof=1 stated

title: Term structure of Merton credit spreads
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, sigma_V, D, r, maturities [K]. DITANYAKAN: spread and PD per maturity. RUMUS: card Core 2-3 for each T. JAWAB: 1) loop T. 2) d1, d2. 3) s(T), PD(T). 4) bp. 5) check s -> 0 as T -> 0 for V > D; hump shape for medium leverage; PD increasing in T for typical firms.

title: Merton comparative statics: leverage and volatility
deliverables: table [grid]: leverage, sigma_V, DD, PD, spread
frame: DIKETAHUI: base V, sigma_V, D, T, r; grids of D/V and sigma_V. DITANYAKAN: DD, PD, spread over grid. RUMUS: card Core 2-3; leverage L = D e^-rT / V. JAWAB: 1) grid loop. 2) compute. 3) table. 4) check PD increasing in leverage and sigma_V, DD decreasing; spread increasing.

title: Merton expected recovery and loss given default
deliverables: per-firm table [N]: PD, expected recovery rate, LGD, expected loss
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, sigma_V, D, T, r. DITANYAKAN: risk-neutral recovery E[V_T | V_T < D]/D and LGD. RUMUS: E[V_T 1{V_T<D}] = V e^{rT} N(-d1); recovery rate = V e^{rT} N(-d1)/(D N(-d2)); LGD = 1 - recovery; expected loss = D N(-d2) - V e^{rT} N(-d1) (at T, undiscounted). JAWAB: 1) d1, d2. 2) recovery. 3) LGD. 4) check B0 = e^-rT [D (1 - PD) + D PD recovery].

title: Black-Cox first-passage default probability
deliverables: per-firm table [N]: first-passage PD, Merton PD
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, sigma_V, barrier K (flat), drift mu or r (and payout q), T. DITANYAKAN: P(min V_t <= K before T). RUMUS: with m = mu - q - sigma^2/2: PD = N((ln(K/V) - mT)/(sigma sqrt T)) + (K/V)^(2m/sigma^2) N((ln(K/V) + mT)/(sigma sqrt T)). JAWAB: 1) m. 2) both terms. 3) PD. 4) compare with Merton N(-d2) using D = K. 5) check first-passage PD >= terminal PD.
formulas: PD = N((ln(K/V) - mT)/(sigma sqrt T)) + (K/V)^(2m/sigma^2) N((ln(K/V) + mT)/(sigma sqrt T))

title: Risky debt as risk-free debt minus a put (credit insurance)
deliverables: per-firm table [N]: put value, risky debt, guarantee cost
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, sigma_V, D, T, r. DITANYAKAN: put on assets with strike D, risky debt value, cost of a guarantee. RUMUS: P = D e^-rT N(-d2) - V N(-d1); B0 = D e^-rT - P; guarantee fee = P (as fraction of D e^-rT if asked). JAWAB: 1) d1, d2. 2) put. 3) B0. 4) check parity E - P = V - D e^-rT.
formulas: P = D e^(-rT) N(-d2) - V N(-d1)

title: Implied asset volatility from an observed credit spread
deliverables: per-firm table [N]: implied sigma_V, repriced spread
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, D, T, r, observed spread s_obs (bp). DITANYAKAN: sigma_V such that Merton spread = s_obs. RUMUS: card Core 3 spread function s(sigma_V); solve s(sigma_V) - s_obs = 0 by brentq on (1e-4, 3). JAWAB: 1) bp -> decimal. 2) residual. 3) bracket check. 4) solve. 5) reprice. 6) check s increasing in sigma_V; no root if s_obs above max -> report.

title: Hazard rate from credit spread (credit triangle)
frame: DIKETAHUI: spread s (bp or decimal), recovery R. DITANYAKAN: flat hazard lambda. RUMUS: card Core 4: lambda = s/(1-R); toolkit hazard_from_spread(spread, recovery). JAWAB: 1) bp -> /10000. 2) R default 40% if missing. 3) lambda. 4) check lambda > 0, increasing in s and R.

title: Default probability over horizon from a spread
frame: DIKETAHUI: spread s, recovery R, horizons T [K]. DITANYAKAN: PD(T) and S(T). RUMUS: card completing: lambda = s/(1-R); S(T) = exp(-lambda T); PD = 1 - exp(-s T/(1-R)); toolkit pd_from_spread(spread, T, recovery). JAWAB: 1) units. 2) lambda. 3) S, PD per T. 4) check PD increasing in T; exponential form not (1-lambda)^T.
pitfalls: discrete (1-lambda)^T survival when continuous is default

title: Survival probability from piecewise-constant hazards
frame: DIKETAHUI: hazard tenors [P] and hazards lambda_k [P], query times t [K]. DITANYAKAN: S(t). RUMUS: card Core 4: S(t) = exp(-sum_k lambda_k (min(t,t_k) - t_{k-1})^+); beyond last tenor extend last lambda; toolkit survival_prob(t, hazard_tenors, hazards). JAWAB: 1) sort tenors. 2) integrated hazard per t. 3) exp. 4) check S decreasing from 1.

title: Interval and conditional default probabilities from a survival curve
deliverables: table [periods]: unconditional PD in (a,b], conditional PD
frame: DIKETAHUI: survival curve S(t) (or hazards), periods (a,b]. DITANYAKAN: unconditional and conditional default probabilities per period. RUMUS: card Core 4: P(a < tau <= b) = S(a) - S(b); conditional = 1 - S(b)/S(a); average hazard = -ln(S(b)/S(a))/(b-a). JAWAB: 1) S at endpoints. 2) differences. 3) ratios. 4) check unconditional sum to 1 - S(T_last).

title: Hazard rate from corporate vs risk-free bond yields
frame: DIKETAHUI: corporate yields y_c and risk-free yields y_f per maturity (percent or decimal), recovery R. DITANYAKAN: average hazard per maturity and cumulative PD. RUMUS: card completing: lambda_bar(T) = (y_c - y_f)/(1-R); PD(T) = 1 - exp(-lambda_bar T); forward hazard between maturities: (lambda_bar_2 T_2 - lambda_bar_1 T_1)/(T_2 - T_1). JAWAB: 1) units (percent points). 2) spreads. 3) hazards. 4) forward hazards. 5) check positive.
pitfalls: percent points vs decimals in the yield difference

title: Bond-implied hazard rate matching a risky bond price
deliverables: summary: flat hazard, PV of expected default loss
frame: DIKETAHUI: coupon bond (face, coupon, frequency, maturity), market price, risk-free curve, recovery as % of face (claim amount). DITANYAKAN: flat lambda reproducing the price. RUMUS: Hull ch.24: price = PV_rf - sum_j q_j DF(t_j)(F_j - R C), q_j = S(t_{j-1}) - S(t_j) on default grid (mid-period), F_j = risk-free forward bond value at t_j. JAWAB: 1) risk-free value. 2) default grid. 3) loss per default time. 4) brentq for lambda. 5) check reprices price.
formulas: P_mkt = P_rf - sum_j (S(t_{j-1}) - S(t_j)) DF(t_j) (F_j - R C)

title: Risk-neutral vs real-world default probability and risk premium
deliverables: table [ratings or names]: lambda_Q, lambda_P, ratio, excess spread
frame: DIKETAHUI: spreads per rating, recovery, historical PDs (or average annual hazard from default studies). DITANYAKAN: risk-neutral hazard, real-world hazard, ratio, spread premium. RUMUS: lambda_Q = s/(1-R); lambda_P = -ln(1-PD_cum(T))/T; expected-loss spread = lambda_P (1-R); premium = s - lambda_P(1-R). JAWAB: 1) units. 2) both hazards. 3) ratio lambda_Q/lambda_P. 4) premium. 5) check ratio > 1 typically.

title: CDS premium and protection legs with flat hazard
deliverables: summary: RPV01, protection PV, par spread (bp)
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda (or spread to convert), R, r (flat) or discount curve, maturity, frequency. DITANYAKAN: RPV01, protection leg PV, par spread. RUMUS: card Core 5: RPV01 = sum Delta_i DF(t_i) S(t_i) [+ accrual]; Prot = (1-R) sum DF(t_i)(S(t_{i-1}) - S(t_i)); par = Prot/RPV01; toolkit cds_legs(hazards, hazard_tenors, maturity, recovery, discount_curve_fn, freq). JAWAB: 1) schedule. 2) DF, S. 3) legs. 4) par. 5) check par ~ lambda(1-R).

title: CDS par spread from a hazard curve
frame: DIKETAHUI: piecewise hazards [P] with tenors, R, discount curve, maturities [K]. DITANYAKAN: par spreads per maturity. RUMUS: card Core 5: par(T) = Prot(T)/RPV01(T); toolkit cds_par_spread(hazards, hazard_tenors, maturity, recovery, discount_curve_fn). JAWAB: 1) for each T: schedule, legs. 2) ratio. 3) bp. 4) check increasing with lambda and 1-R; flat hazard -> par ~ lambda(1-R).

title: CDS with accrued premium on default
deliverables: summary: RPV01 with and without accrual, par spreads
frame: DIKETAHUI: hazards, R, discount curve, maturity, freq; task asks accrual. DITANYAKAN: legs and par spread with accrual. RUMUS: card Core 5, V4 (a): RPV01 = sum Delta_i DF(t_i) S(t_i) + sum (Delta_i/2) DF(t_i)(S(t_{i-1}) - S(t_i)). JAWAB: 1) schedule. 2) both terms. 3) par = Prot/RPV01. 4) compare to no-accrual. 5) check accrual lowers par slightly.
formulas: RPV01_acc = sum Delta_i DF_i S_i + sum (Delta_i/2) DF_i (S_{i-1} - S_i)
pitfalls: accrual included when task says simple textbook / none

title: Bootstrapping a piecewise hazard curve from CDS quotes
deliverables: table [P]: tenor, spread, hazard, survival at tenor
frame: DIKETAHUI: CDS quotes [P] (tenor years, spread bp), R, discount curve, freq, accrual flag. DITANYAKAN: lambda_k [P], S(t_k). RUMUS: card Core 6: for tenors in increasing order solve lambda_k (brentq [1e-8, 5]) so PV(tenor k at its par) = 0 with earlier lambdas fixed; toolkit cds_bootstrap(tenors, spreads, recovery, discount_curve_fn, freq, accrual). JAWAB: 1) sort, convert bp. 2) sequential solves. 3) survival. 4) reprice EVERY quote. 5) report negative hazards, do not floor silently.
pitfalls: unsorted tenors break the sequential solve

title: CDS bootstrap with an interpolated zero curve
frame: DIKETAHUI: zero rates at pillars [K] (compounding stated), CDS quotes, R. DITANYAKAN: hazards with DF at payment dates. RUMUS: card completing: DF(t) by linear interpolation in zero rate (or log-DF linear) - state which; flat extrapolation; DF = exp(-z t) continuous. JAWAB: 1) build discount_curve_fn. 2) check DF(0)=1, decreasing. 3) bootstrap. 4) reprice.

title: CDS upfront from standard coupon
frame: DIKETAHUI: par spread s_par (or hazard), standard coupon c (100/500 bp), R, curve, notional. DITANYAKAN: upfront paid by protection buyer. RUMUS: card Core 5: upfront = (s_par - c) RPV01 (fraction of notional); with flat hazard from s_par. JAWAB: 1) hazard from s_par (flat via bootstrap or credit triangle as stated). 2) RPV01. 3) upfront. 4) x notional. 5) sign: positive -> buyer pays.

title: Converting an upfront quote to an equivalent par spread
deliverables: summary: implied flat hazard, par spread (bp)
frame: DIKETAHUI: upfront U (fraction), coupon c, R, curve, maturity. DITANYAKAN: flat hazard and par spread. RUMUS: solve lambda: Prot(lambda) - c RPV01(lambda) = U; then s_par = Prot/RPV01. JAWAB: 1) residual(lambda). 2) brentq. 3) par spread. 4) check U = (s_par - c) RPV01 at solution.

title: CDS mark-to-market for protection buyer
frame: DIKETAHUI: existing contract spread s_c, current market spreads/hazard curve, R, curve, remaining maturity, notional. DITANYAKAN: buyer MTM. RUMUS: card Core 5: MTM_buyer = (s_mkt - s_c) RPV01_mkt x notional; seller = -MTM. JAWAB: 1) bootstrap current curve. 2) RPV01 for remaining schedule. 3) MTM. 4) check positive when spreads widened.

title: CS01 / spread DV01 of a CDS
frame: DIKETAHUI: CDS position (contract spread, notional), market quotes, R, curve. DITANYAKAN: change in MTM for +1 bp parallel bump of quotes. RUMUS: CS01 = MTM(quotes + 1bp) - MTM(quotes) with re-bootstrapped hazards; approximation CS01 ~ RPV01 x 1e-4 x notional. JAWAB: 1) base bootstrap and MTM. 2) bump all quotes by 1e-4. 3) re-bootstrap. 4) new MTM. 5) difference; compare approximation.

title: Recovery rate sensitivity of a bootstrapped curve
deliverables: table [recoveries]: hazards, survival at maturity, MTM
frame: DIKETAHUI: CDS quotes, recovery grid [K], curve. DITANYAKAN: hazards, survival and MTM per recovery. RUMUS: card Core 4-6: holding par spreads fixed, lambda ~ s/(1-R) rises with R; par-quoted contract MTM nearly unchanged; upfront-quoted contracts change. JAWAB: 1) loop R. 2) bootstrap. 3) survival. 4) MTM. 5) check survival decreasing in R.

title: ISDA standard CDS schedule (IMM dates, ACT/360)
deliverables: table [payments]: date, year fraction, DF, survival
frame: DIKETAHUI: trade date, maturity (standard IMM), coupon, R, curves. DITANYAKAN: payment schedule and RPV01 under ISDA conventions. RUMUS: card conventions: payments 20 Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec, Delta = days/360, accrued-on-default included, R = 40% senior unsecured. JAWAB: 1) generate IMM dates up to maturity. 2) year fractions ACT/360 (time for DF in ACT/365). 3) DF, S. 4) RPV01 with accrual. 5) check Delta ~ 0.25.
pitfalls: using ACT/360 fractions also as the time axis for DF and survival

title: Negative hazard detection in an inverted CDS curve
frame: DIKETAHUI: CDS quotes with steeply inverted shape. DITANYAKAN: hazards and validity. RUMUS: card pitfalls: bootstrap allowing negative bracket (e.g. [-1, 5]) to find the root; negative lambda_k => S increasing => arbitrage; report, do not floor unless told. JAWAB: 1) bootstrap with widened bracket. 2) flag lambda_k < 0. 3) if task says floor, set 0 and report repricing error. 4) check reprice.

title: Forward CDS spread between two maturities
frame: DIKETAHUI: hazard curve (or quotes), R, curve, T1 < T2. DITANYAKAN: forward-starting CDS spread. RUMUS: s_fwd = (Prot(T2) - Prot(T1))/(RPV01(T2) - RPV01(T1)) = (s2 RPV01_2 - s1 RPV01_1)/(RPV01_2 - RPV01_1). JAWAB: 1) legs to T1, T2 on common schedule. 2) differences. 3) ratio. 4) bp. 5) check between s1 and s2 extrapolated beyond s2 if curve steep.

title: CDS-bond basis
deliverables: table [bonds]: CDS spread, bond spread, basis (bp)
frame: DIKETAHUI: CDS par spread at bond maturity (interpolate), bond z-spread or asset-swap spread. DITANYAKAN: basis. RUMUS: basis = s_CDS - s_bond (bp); negative basis -> buy bond + buy protection. JAWAB: 1) interpolate CDS to bond maturity. 2) bond spread (z-spread over swap curve). 3) basis. 4) sign interpretation.

title: Z-spread of a risky coupon bond
frame: DIKETAHUI: bond cash flows, dirty price, zero curve. DITANYAKAN: constant spread z such that discounted CFs = price. RUMUS: P = sum CF_t exp(-(z_rf(t) + z) t) (continuous) or matching the curve compounding. JAWAB: 1) cash flows. 2) residual(z). 3) brentq. 4) bp. 5) check reprices; z > 0 for risky issuer.
formulas: P = sum_t CF_t exp(-(r(t) + z) t)
pitfalls: clean price used when dirty price needed

title: Risky zero-coupon bond price under recovery conventions
deliverables: table [maturities]: price under each convention, yield spread
frame: DIKETAHUI: flat lambda (or survival curve), R, risk-free r, maturities. DITANYAKAN: risky ZCB price and spread. RUMUS: RT: B = e^-rT [S(T) + R(1-S(T))]; RMV: B = e^-(r + lambda(1-R))T; RF: B = e^-rT S(T) + R int_0^T e^-ru f(u) du with f = lambda S. JAWAB: 1) S. 2) price per convention. 3) spread = -(1/T) ln(B/e^-rT). 4) check RMV spread = lambda(1-R) exactly.

title: Longstaff-Mithal-Neis spread decomposition (default vs non-default)
deliverables: table [bonds or dates]: yield spread, CDS, non-default, default share
frame: DIKETAHUI: bond yields, risk-free/swap yields (percent points), CDS spreads (bp), aligned dates. DITANYAKAN: default and non-default components and shares. RUMUS: card Core 8: default = CDS; non-default = (y_bond - y_rf) - CDS; share = default/total x100. JAWAB: 1) units to bp (pp x100). 2) align by date/maturity. 3) components. 4) shares. 5) means over time.

title: Expected-loss component of spreads (Elton et al)
deliverables: table [ratings]: spread, expected-loss part, premium, share
frame: DIKETAHUI: spreads per rating/maturity, physical PDs (annual or cumulative), recovery. DITANYAKAN: expected-loss spread and remainder. RUMUS: card Core 8: EL spread ~ lambda_P (1-R), lambda_P = -ln(1-PD_cum(T))/T; premium = spread - EL spread (tax/liquidity/risk premium). JAWAB: 1) PD to hazard. 2) EL spread bp. 3) remainder. 4) share EL/spread. 5) check EL share small for IG.

title: Regression decomposition of spread changes into factor shares
frame: DIKETAHUI: spread changes Y [T], factors X [T x K]. DITANYAKAN: coefficients and percent contribution per factor. RUMUS: card Core 8: OLS with intercept (toolkit ols(y, X)); pct_k = Cov(b_k X_k, Y)/Var(Y) x 100; sum pct_k = 100 R^2; residual share = 100(1-R^2). JAWAB: 1) align, drop NaN. 2) OLS. 3) covariances with same ddof as Var. 4) shares. 5) check sum + residual = 100.
pitfalls: mixed ddof between Cov and Var

title: Newey-West HAC standard errors for spread regressions
deliverables: table [coefficients]: estimate, NW se, t, p
frame: DIKETAHUI: Y [T], X [T x K], lag m. DITANYAKAN: OLS coefficients with HAC errors. RUMUS: card Core 9: S = G0 + sum_{j=1..m} (1 - j/(m+1))(G_j + G_j'); V = (X'X)^-1 S (X'X)^-1; toolkit ols(y, X, hac_lags=m). JAWAB: 1) design with constant. 2) residuals. 3) G_j. 4) V. 5) se, t, p (normal or t as stated). 6) check vs statsmodels cov_type='HAC' with use_correction matching.
pitfalls: small-sample T/(T-k) factor added when raw sandwich is asked

title: Newey-West t-statistic of a mean spread change
frame: DIKETAHUI: series x [T] (spread changes or basis), lags m. DITANYAKAN: HAC t-stat of mean. RUMUS: card Core 9 with X = 1: LRV = g0 + 2 sum_j (1 - j/(m+1)) g_j, g_j = (1/T) sum e_t e_{t-j}; se = sqrt(LRV/T); t = mean/se; toolkit newey_west_tstat(series, lags). JAWAB: 1) demean. 2) autocovariances. 3) LRV. 4) t. 5) check m = 0 gives ordinary t (with 1/T variance).

title: Automatic Newey-West lag selection
deliverables: summary: chosen lag m, HAC results
frame: DIKETAHUI: series length T, task silent on lags. DITANYAKAN: lag and HAC statistics. RUMUS: card Core 9: m = floor(4 (T/100)^(2/9)). JAWAB: 1) T after dropping NaN. 2) m. 3) HAC estimate. 4) state lag used.
pitfalls: T counted before dropping missing rows

title: FRED yield data alignment to monthly spreads
frame: DIKETAHUI: FRED CSVs (dates, yields in percent points, '.' for missing), possibly daily and monthly. DITANYAKAN: monthly spread series and stats. RUMUS: card pitfalls: to_numeric(errors='coerce'); monthly = last valid observation per month; forward-fill discontinued series before dropping; spread_bp = (y1 - y2) x 100. JAWAB: 1) parse. 2) resample month-end last. 3) join. 4) drop NaN rows; window by rows after dropping. 5) bp.

title: Unilateral CVA from expected exposure profile
deliverables: table [t]: EE, DF, PD increment, CVA term
frame: DIKETAHUI: EE profile [n] at times t_i, counterparty hazards or spreads, R, discount curve. DITANYAKAN: CVA. RUMUS: card Core 7: CVA = (1-R) sum DF(t_i) EE(t_i) [S(t_{i-1}) - S(t_i)]. JAWAB: 1) survival from hazards (credit triangle if spreads). 2) PD increments. 3) DF. 4) sum. 5) check CVA >= 0, <= (1-R) max EE.
pitfalls: EE at period start vs end: follow stated convention or midpoint

title: EE, PFE and EPE from simulated exposure paths
frame: DIKETAHUI: MTM paths V [n_paths x n_times], times, level q. DITANYAKAN: EE(t), PFE(t), EPE. RUMUS: card Core 7: E+ = max(V,0); EE = mean E+; PFE_q = quantile(E+, q); ENE = mean max(-V,0); EPE = time-average of EE (trapezoid over horizon / T). JAWAB: 1) positive part. 2) column stats. 3) EPE. 4) check EE >= 0, PFE >= EE for high q.

title: Analytic EE of a forward contract and CVA
frame: DIKETAHUI: forward on asset S (sigma, r, q), delivery K, maturity T, counterparty hazard, R. DITANYAKAN: EE at t and CVA. RUMUS: value at t: V_t = (F_t - K) e^-r(T-t); discounted EE(t) = e^-rT E[(F_t - K)^+] = Black call on F with vol sigma sqrt t: e^-rT [F0 N(d1) - K N(d2)], d1 = [ln(F0/K) + sigma^2 t/2]/(sigma sqrt t); CVA = (1-R) sum disc EE(t_i) PD_i. JAWAB: 1) grid. 2) EE. 3) PD increments. 4) CVA.
formulas: disc EE(t) = e^(-rT) [F0 N(d1(t)) - K N(d2(t))]

title: Bilateral CVA (CVA minus DVA)
frame: DIKETAHUI: EE and ENE profiles, counterparty and own hazards/spreads, recoveries. DITANYAKAN: CVA, DVA, BCVA. RUMUS: card Core 7: CVA = (1-R_c) sum DF EE dPD_c; DVA = (1-R_own) sum DF ENE dPD_own (ENE = E[max(-V,0)]); BCVA = CVA - DVA (first-to-default ignored unless stated: then weight by other party survival). JAWAB: 1) survivals. 2) legs. 3) difference. 4) check DVA >= 0.

title: Netting and collateral effects on exposure
deliverables: table [t]: EE gross, EE netted, EE collateralised
frame: DIKETAHUI: trade-level MTM paths [n_trades x n_paths x n_times], collateral threshold H, MPR lag. DITANYAKAN: exposure and CVA with/without netting and collateral. RUMUS: gross EE = E[sum_k max(V_k,0)]; netted EE = E[max(sum_k V_k, 0)]; collateralised E = max(V_t - C_t, 0), C_t = max(V_{t-MPR} - H, 0). JAWAB: 1) aggregate. 2) collateral with lag. 3) EE each. 4) CVA each. 5) check netted <= gross.

title: Wrong-way risk CVA (exposure correlated with default)
deliverables: summary: independent CVA, wrong-way CVA, ratio
frame: DIKETAHUI: exposure driver paths, counterparty hazard, R, correlation rho between driver shock and default variable, n_paths, seed. DITANYAKAN: CVA with dependence. RUMUS: default time tau = S^-1(Phi(Z_d)), Z_d correlated with exposure driver; CVA = (1-R) E[DF(tau) max(V_tau,0) 1{tau <= T}]. JAWAB: 1) correlated normals. 2) default times. 3) exposure at default interval. 4) average. 5) compare rho = 0 (same seed). 6) check WWR CVA > independent for positive dependence.

title: CVA expressed as a running spread
frame: DIKETAHUI: CVA, trade notional, maturity, counterparty survival, curve. DITANYAKAN: CVA as running spread. RUMUS: s_CVA = CVA/(N RPV01) (risky annuity of counterparty); approximation s_CVA ~ EPE x s_cpty / N. JAWAB: 1) RPV01. 2) ratio. 3) bp. 4) compare approximation.

title: Effective EE and EEPE (Basel IMM)
frame: DIKETAHUI: EE profile at dates within one year. DITANYAKAN: effective EE, EEPE, EAD. RUMUS: EffEE(t_k) = max(EffEE(t_{k-1}), EE(t_k)); EEPE = sum_{t_k <= 1y} EffEE(t_k) Delta_k / (sum Delta_k); EAD = alpha EEPE, alpha = 1.4. JAWAB: 1) running max. 2) weighted average to min(1y, maturity). 3) EAD. 4) check EffEE non-decreasing.

title: Merton-implied vs CDS-implied PD comparison across firms
frame: DIKETAHUI: per firm: E, sigma_E, D, T, r and CDS spread, R. DITANYAKAN: both PDs and their association. RUMUS: card Core 1-2 (PD = N(-d2)); CDS: PD = 1 - exp(-s T/(1-R)). JAWAB: 1) calibrate Merton per firm. 2) PD_merton. 3) PD_cds. 4) ratio, Pearson and Spearman correlation. 5) check same horizon T in both.

title: Equity elasticity and leverage effect in Merton
deliverables: per-firm table [N]: delta, elasticity, sigma_E implied
frame: DIKETAHUI: V, sigma_V, D, T, r. DITANYAKAN: dE/dV, elasticity Omega = N(d1) V/E, implied equity vol. RUMUS: card Core 1: dE/dV = N(d1); sigma_E = N(d1) sigma_V V/E; dB/dV = 1 - N(d1). JAWAB: 1) d1. 2) E. 3) delta, elasticity. 4) sigma_E. 5) check sigma_E > sigma_V, elasticity > 1, rising with leverage.

title: CDS index / portfolio average hazard from constituent spreads
deliverables: summary: intrinsic index spread, quoted index spread, basis
frame: DIKETAHUI: constituent CDS spreads [n], R, curve, maturity, quoted index spread. DITANYAKAN: intrinsic spread and index basis. RUMUS: intrinsic s_I = sum_k s_k RPV01_k / sum_k RPV01_k (RPV01-weighted); simple average as approximation; basis = s_quoted - s_I. JAWAB: 1) flat hazards per name. 2) RPV01_k. 3) weighted average. 4) basis. 5) check s_I <= simple average when dispersion high.
formulas: s_I = sum_k s_k RPV01_k / sum_k RPV01_k
